question.worked_solution:
If we let $u=3x,$ then 

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{3}\text{d}u.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives

| $x$ | $0$ | $\pi /3$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $\pi $ |

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}2\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }2\operatorname{cos}⁡u\cdot \frac{1}{3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{2}{3}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡u\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡u{|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡0) \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$
